The region $D$ in the upper-half plane is enclosed between two semi-circles centered at $O$ of radii $1$ and $2,$ as shown above. What is
${∬}_{D}(x-y)\,\text{d}A$
expressed in polar coordinates?
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form 

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

The region $D$ represents a portion of the washer enclosed between the circles of radii $1$ and $2$ centered at the origin. In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,0\le \theta \le \pi }.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(x-y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={∬}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{2}r(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
